A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfiFPO work and contain readable text, equations, two figures, sixteen tables, and Appendices A–F. The increase from 21 to 22 pages reflects reflow, with no missing comparative material.

before.justification: v2 reports original InfiFPO benchmark results in Table 2, ablations in Section 4, and supplementary experiments and case studies in Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark, ablation, scaling, and case-study outcomes in Section 4 and Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The InfiFPO objective, sequence-level fusion, length normalization, probability clipping, max-margin selection, and adaptations to WRPO and IPO are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain Infinity-Instruct, NuminaMath-1.5, KodCode-V1-SFT, supplementary UltraFeedback training, and the same eleven evaluation benchmarks and case-study tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains FuseLLM, FuseChat, InfiFusion, SFT, SFT-DPO, SFT-IPO, and SFT-WRPO. Comparator membership also matches within the corresponding appendix experiments.

E3.justification: Both retain half-data SFT for three epochs followed by half-data preference optimization for one epoch. Source and pivot configurations, sampling settings, evaluation prompts, and appendix experimental protocols also match.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 and Appendices E–F retain the same fusion-strategy comparisons, component and source-count ablations, reward-model sensitivity, sequence-alignment and scaling analyses, and code/math case studies.

E5.justification: Both use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports experimental run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 reports averages of 79.95 for Phi-4 and 83.33 for InfiFPO in both versions; Figure 2 and the supplementary result entries are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, gradient analysis, and derivations in Section 3 and Appendices A, C, and D are unchanged. Equations move across pages without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about implicit sequence-level fusion, stabilization strategies, efficiency, benchmark performance, and compatibility with other preference objectives.

C2.justification: Interpretations of knowledge transfer, fusion strategies, ablations, and case studies remain unchanged, as do the stated theoretical and computational limitations. Appendix F discussion moves relative to its tables without changing meaning.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters and hardware, Appendix B prompt templates, Appendix E.2 vLLM precomputation and memory details, and project-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 49 references and related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning against WRPO, token-level fusion, model merging, and knowledge distillation.

P1.justification: v3 adds '(PolyU)' to the university name and adds Hongxia Yang's PolyU-Daya Bay Technology and Innovation Research Institute affiliation. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Page reflow relocates existing displays: Table 4 moves from page 8 to page 9, and Tables 15–16 move from pages 20–21 to pages 21–22. Figure designs, table structures, and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 updates institutional attribution and reflows existing material, including appendix tables. The scientific evidence, reasoning, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, and the layout shifts do not establish a meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
